action_history.rationale: Model: Sum of 10 pseudo-Voigt components + constant offset on weak-ALS baseline-corrected Raman spectrum (baseline added back for raw-space overlay); two components reallocated to real bands at ~1210 and ~1240 cm-1 with amplitude/FWHM lower bounds; nu1 modeled by single sharp high-eta Lorentzian-leaning core

result.detailed_analysis: The spectrum is unambiguously a CO3(2-) carbonate: the strongest band at 1084.9 cm-1 is the nu1 symmetric stretch; the pair at 701.3/705.6 cm-1 is the nu4 in-plane bend; bands below 300 cm-1 (142.9, 189.5, 213.4, 272.0, 283.7) are external/lattice (translational and librational) modes; the weak broad features at 1206 and 1238 cm-1 fall in the 2nu2/combination region. Applying the mandatory carbonate disambiguation: calcite presents nu1 at 1086, a SINGLE nu4 near 712, and lattice modes at 282/156, whereas aragonite presents nu1 at ~1085, a nu4 DOUBLET at 705+701, and lattice modes near 206 and 152. The observed data contain a clearly resolved nu4 doublet (701.3 and 705.6 cm-1, ~4 cm-1 apart) and prominent lattice modes at ~190 and ~213 cm-1, together with a lower-frequency mode at ~143 cm-1. This pattern is consistent with ARAGONITE (orthorhombic CaCO3), not calcite. The fitted band positions match aragonite across the three strongest features (nu1, nu4 doublet, lattice cluster), satisfying the requirement that a candidate explain the top bands with multiple matches rather than snapping the strongest line to calcite. The nu1 modeling is imperfect: the dispersive residual indicates the true lineshape has a sharper core and/or heavier wings than a single pseudo-Voigt, so the fitted FWHM (3.30 cm-1) is an effective value and the integrated area/relative intensities carry systematic error near this band. Because no chemistry (EDX/XRF) was provided, this is a pattern-only identification; Ca is inferred from the carbonate polymorph pattern, not measured. Compact band summary (center cm-1, relative intensity, strongest first): 1084.9 (1.00), 701.3 (0.128), 705.6 (0.085), 213.4 (0.080), 1238.1 (0.059), 189.5 (0.047), 1206.3 (0.042), 272.0 (0.024), 283.7 (0.022), 142.9 (0.014).

scientific_claims.claim: The spectrum matches aragonite (orthorhombic CaCO3): CO3 nu1 at 1084.9 cm-1, a resolved nu4 doublet at 701.3 and 705.6 cm-1, and lattice modes at ~189.5 and ~213.4 cm-1 (positions from fit; formal uncertainties not computed).
scientific_claims.scientific_impact: Distinguishing aragonite from calcite by the nu4 doublet and lattice-mode pattern (rather than the shared ~1085 cm-1 nu1) is central to biomineral, paleoclimate, and diagenesis studies where polymorph identity records formation environment and post-depositional alteration.
scientific_claims.has_anyone_question: Has anyone confirmed aragonite via the resolved 701/705 cm-1 nu4 doublet and sub-220 cm-1 lattice modes as the discriminant against calcite in this sample type?

verification_iterations.model: Sum of pseudo-Voigt profiles on a near-zero linear residual baseline. Components (10 total): (1) ~190 cm⁻¹ lattice mode, (2) ~215 cm⁻¹ lattice mode, (3) ~272 cm⁻¹ (doublet partner), (4) ~284 cm⁻¹ (doublet partner), (5) ~701 cm⁻¹ (doublet partner), (6) ~706 cm⁻¹ (doublet partner), (7) ~1086 cm⁻¹ strong symmetric stretch (ν1), (8) ~1100 cm⁻¹ shoulder, (9) ~1210 cm⁻¹, (10) ~1240 cm⁻¹. Each pseudo-Voigt: A·[η·L(x;x0,w) + (1-η)·G(x;x0,w)]. Baseline: ALS (asymmetric least squares) subtraction applied prior to fitting.

issues.problem: Dominant peak severely under-resolved; single pseudo-Voigt cannot capture the sharp cusp plus broad wings
A clearly real data maximum at ~143 (intensity ~350) is completely unmodeled
Oscillating residuals indicate peak-shape mismatch / unresolved shoulder near the 213 peak

verification_iterations.fix_applied: Reseed component centers within the fixed 10-component budget: add coverage at ~143, add a broad pedestal component near ~1085 (reallocating the near-zero-amplitude peak_8 at 1105), and refine eta/width around 213-225.

verification_iterations.model: Sum of 10 pseudo-Voigt profiles on a near-zero linear residual baseline (ALS-subtracted). Each pseudo-Voigt: A·[η·L(x;x0,w) + (1-η)·G(x;x0,w)]. The 10-component budget is preserved but reallocated to match verified features: (1) ~143 cm⁻¹ lattice mode (reallocated from former spurious peak_8 at 1105); (2) ~190 cm⁻¹ lattice mode; (3) ~213 cm⁻¹ lattice mode (eta/width refined for shape mismatch); (4) ~222 cm⁻¹ shoulder (reseeded near 220-225 to capture unresolved partner); (5) ~272 cm⁻¹ doublet partner; (6) ~284 cm⁻¹ doublet partner; (7) ~1086 cm⁻¹ SHARP ν1 symmetric-stretch core (narrow, more Lorentzian, high η); (8) ~1085 cm⁻¹ BROAD pedestal under ν1 (wide, lower η, shares total intensity with component 7); (9) ~701 cm⁻¹ doublet partner; (10) ~706 cm⁻¹ doublet partner. Note: with the budget locked at 10, the 1210/1240 broad humps and one of the 700-region partners are subsumed — priority is given to the verified real features (143, ν1 core+pedestal, 220-225 shoulder). The dominant ν1 line is now explicitly modeled as a two-component narrow-core + broad-pedestal pair rather than a single profile.

issues.problem: Two clearly real data maxima (~1210 intensity ~1080, ~1240 intensity ~1400) are essentially unmodeled — the fit places only a flat near-baseline curve here

The intended narrow-core + broad-pedestal decomposition collapsed: peak_8 (pedestal) refined to near-zero amplitude (0.006), so the sharp cusp plus broad wings are still described by a single narrow profile
Rising shoulder / onset of the 1210 band is not captured

verification_iterations.fix_applied: Reallocate the collapsed peak_4 and peak_8: seed one component at ~1210 and one at ~1240 cm⁻¹ to recover those bands, and give the ~1085 broad pedestal a nonzero starting FWHM/amplitude so the narrow-core+pedestal split actually forms.

verification_iterations.model: Sum of 10 pseudo-Voigt profiles on a near-zero linear residual baseline (ALS-subtracted). Each pseudo-Voigt: A·[η·L(x;x0,w) + (1-η)·G(x;x0,w)]. The 10-component budget is preserved but REALLOCATED based on verification feedback to prioritize verified real data maxima. Two components previously collapsed to zero (peak_4, A~1.5e-5; and peak_8, the intended pedestal at A~0.006) are reclaimed and reassigned to the two clearly real, currently-unmodeled bands at ~1210 and ~1240 cm⁻¹. Component allocation: (1) ~143 cm⁻¹ lattice mode; (2) ~190 cm⁻¹ lattice mode; (3) ~213 cm⁻¹ lattice mode (eta/width refined for shape mismatch); (4) ~1210 cm⁻¹ broad band (REALLOCATED from collapsed peak_4; seed intensity ~1080) — its rising low-frequency wing also covers the 1130-1200 shoulder onset; (5) ~272 cm⁻¹ doublet partner; (6) ~284 cm⁻¹ doublet partner; (7) ~1086 cm⁻¹ SHARP ν1 symmetric-stretch core (narrow, more Lorentzian, high η); (8) ~1240 cm⁻¹ broad band (REALLOCATED from collapsed peak_8; seed intensity ~1400); (9) ~701 cm⁻¹ doublet partner; (10) ~706 cm⁻¹ doublet partner. TRADE-OFF NOTE: because the collapsed pedestal component (former peak_8) is now reassigned to the ~1240 real band, the ν1 line is modeled by the single sharp core (component 7) with η freed toward strong Lorentzian character to capture both the cusp and the wings via a heavy-tailed Lorentzian profile; the 220-225 shoulder and one 700-region partner remain subsumed since verified real bands at 1210/1240 take priority over the collapsed narrow-core+pedestal split. The ~222 shoulder is absorbed into the refined ~213 component width/eta.

issues.problem: The single sharp core (peak_7) slightly misplaces/underfits the extreme cusp, leaving a derivative-shaped residual spike (data peak ~22000, residual ~±2000).
Low-amplitude wavy residuals (~±100 on signals up to ~1900) with several sign-changes.
